subject: Mythology
title: Medusa: The Gorgon's Gaze
description: A micro-lesson that makes Medusa: The Gorgon's Gaze usable.

hook.text: Medusa could turn anyone to stone with a single look. She was killed by a hero who fought using only a mirror.

buildup.text: She was once a beautiful woman. Athena cursed her after Poseidon assaulted her in Athena's own temple.

discovery.text: Perseus used a polished shield as a mirror to find Medusa without meeting her eyes, then cut off her head.

twist.text: Modern readers see Medusa as a victim, not a villain. She was punished for being attacked, not for any crime.

climax.text: Medusa's image now appears on Versace logos, feminist art, and abuse survivor symbols — completely reinterpreted.

punchline.text: The monster the Greeks created became a symbol of justice they never intended.

quiz.question: Why was Medusa cursed in the original Greek myth?
options: She challenged Athena to a beauty contest
Athena punished her after Poseidon assaulted her in Athena's temple
She stole a sacred artifact from the gods
